segments.he: והנה ענין תיקון הנ״ל כולל את הכל, כי גם הכהנים אשר אין יכולין לבא ולהשתטח על קברי הצדיקים אם צריכין להאהיל גם על קברים אחרים הקבורים אצלם, או לעבור על קברים אחרים עד שבאים לשם שבזה פשיטא דאין להקל אך כבר מבואר במקום אחר באריכות דלענין הכהנים או שאר בני אדם שיש להם אונס אחר עד שאי אפשר להם בשום אופן לבא על קבר הצדיק בעצמו, הדבר ברור שקדושת קבר הצדיק ובפרט הצדיק הגדול במעלה שהוא מבני עלי׳ המופלגים בוודאי קדושת קברו מתפשט בכל הרואה, שמי שבא סמוך לבית הקברות וזוכה לראות ולהסתכל משם על מקום קדושת גניזתו ומקשר לבו וכוונתו אליו ונשען בזכותו ומתפלל ומרבה בתחנונים ושופך כמים לבו נוכח פני ה׳. בוודאי זוכה להמשיך כשלימות כל התיקונים הנפלאים שנמשכין ע״י קדושת קברי הצדיקים עצהיו״ט, כמו אלו שזוכין להתפלל בהשתטחות על קברו ממש ויש ע״ז ראיות ברורות מש״ס ופוסקים, וידוע שכן נהגו הכהנים הק׳ שהיו מתלמידי הבעש״ט ז״ל (כגון הרב מפולנאה השתטחות וכיוצא בבואם על קבר הבעש״ט ז״ל) ובפרט בזמן קהלה לכל כגון בער״ה, (כאשר נציג בסוף הספר) וכן בשאר הימים שיש איזה קיבוץ שמרביץ בתפלה על מקום קדושת גניזתם ז״ל, שאז בוודאי גם תפלת היחיד העומד מרחוק קצת נכללת ג״ב בתוך תפלת הצבור ועושה פעולתה בשלימוח וידוע מארז׳׳ל שהצדיקים מתדמין ליוצרם, ואצל השי״ת נאמר ״האלוקי מקרוב אני נאום ה׳ ולא אלוקי מרחוק״, וארז״ל, אפי׳ מחיצה של ברזל אינה מפסקת בין ישראל לאביהם שבשמים. בוודאי מי שאפשר לו לבא על מקום גניזתו בעצמו ולנשק את עפרו, בוודאי מחויב להשתדל בזה בכל האפשר, אבל הכהנים שהתורה גדרה בעדם שיעמדו מרחוק מחמת י קדושת כהונתם בוודאי אין בזה שום חשש ועיכוב כלל רק אדרבא ואדרבא וכו/ ואין כאן מקום להאריך בזה כ״כ. ובפרט שענין ההשתטחות על קברי הצדיקים ולכוון בזה כוונות ויהודים כידוע, דבר זה אינו נוהג בזמנינו כלל כי אם אפשר ליחידי סגולה המופלגים במעלה מאד, כי כבר ידוע ומפורסם מה שצור, האר״י ז״ל לתלמידיו הק׳ לבלתי לעסוק בזה אחר פטירתו ובפרט בזמנינו ואין לני רק לכוון כפשוטו להרבות שם בתפלה ותחנונים בזכות הצדיקים ולעורר רחמים שם אצל הצדיקים בעצמם שיתפללו בעדינו ויעוררו רחמים גדולים אצל השי״ת עלינו ועל כל ישראל. ולדבר זה אין עיקר גידול ההשתטחות רק ההתקרבות וההשתדלות בזה במחשבה דיבור ומעשה בפועל ממש, וכל מי שבא ביגיעה והשתדלות וטילטול הדרך וחסרון כים וכיוצא בשאר מניעות כאלו והוא משבר הכל בשביל להמשיך עליו איזה התנוצצות והארה מקדושת הצדיק וזכותו הק׳ אע״פ שכבר נסתלק, והגם שא״א לו להשתטח על קברו ממש אעפ״כ כדאי הכל אצלו בכדי לבא עכ״פ למקום הסמוך •:יקברו הק׳ ומסתכל בעיניו ומכוון את לבו ומקשר מחשבתו לקדושת הצדיק השוכן שם, בוודאי מתפשט קדושת הציון הק׳ בכל הרואה, ואף אם יעמוד מרחוק יוכל לבקש שם כל הבקשות, ולהרבות שם בתחנונים על כל הצריך אליו ובוודאי תתקבל תפלתו, וכן יהיו כא..(חסר) זה יל התיקונים הקדושים כמו מי שנשתטח והרבה בתחנונים על קבר הצדיק ממש: (ועיין מ״ר נשא פרשה יד) שבשכר שעיקם יוסף את עיניו מלהסתכל באשת פוטיפר ולא במצריות וכר אמר הקב״ה עלי לשלם שכר אותה העין כיצד שנו רבותינו שהיו אוכלים במקדש קדשים קלים תוך החומה לפנים מחומת ירושלים, אבל שילה שהי׳ בחלק יוסף אוכלין בכל הרואה וכר וכן אמרו רז״ל ג״כ (בזבחים קיח:) ומזה מובן גם לענין קדושת קבר הצדיק האמת שהוא בחי׳ יוסף שעיקר מעלת קדושתו הוא כפי מעלת ומדריגת הדושתו בקדושת הברית, שעיקר תלוי בקדושת העינים וכמבואר במקום אחר, והצדיק הגדול שזכה לקדושת הברית ולקדושת העינים בתכלית השליטות בפרט זה הצדיק שזכה להתפאר שאין לו שום הסתכלות בזה העולם וכו׳ וכמבואר במ״א והודיע בעצמו קצת מגודל מעלת קדושת קברו הק׳. והבטיח וכר וכו׳ כנ״ל, בוודאי שקדושת קברו תופס בכל הרואה וככל הנ״ל: ויש עוד להאריך כזה הרבה ולחזק הענין מכל צד איבעית אימא קרא ומרז״ל ואי בעית אימא סברא אך אין כאן מקום לזה. וכ״ז לענין קדושת התיקונים שנמשכין ע״י אמירת תהלים ושאר תחנונים ובקשות על מקום גניזתו הק׳ שעוסקים בזה בכל ימות השנה ובפרט בימי אלול הק׳. אבל ענין מה שנהגו מימי קדם וכן עכשיו ולדורות עולם אי״ה להתקבץ יחד על ר״ה הקדוש וקודם ד״ה ובפרט בער״ה מרבין באמירת תהלים ותחינות ובקשות ותשובה ותפלה וצדקה במקום גניזתו הק׳ ואח״כ מתפללין כל הקיבוץ ביחד בר״זד, וזה הענין עולה על כולנה ונעשין עי״ז דברים ותיקונים גבוהים נפלאים ונוראים מאד וכמובן מדבריו ז״ל בפרט בס׳ ״ליקוטי הלכות״׳ הק׳ כי מלבד קדושת ההשתטחות והתפלות שמתפללין על ציונו הק׳ שבדבר זה את הכל שוין וכחנים מחיצה לעצמן כנ״ל מלבד זה נעשין תיקונים נפלאים ע״י קדושת הקיבוץ שמתקבצין להתפלל ביחד בר״ה בביה״כ הק׳ שנקראת על שמו ז״ל, ובדבר זה כולם שוים כהנים לוים וישראלים וכו׳. ויתבאר עוד מזה במ״א אי״ה (ועי׳ בזוה״ק שמות ד׳ ה׳.) מה שאמר ר׳ חייא לר׳ יוסי, אי בני עלמא הווי ידעי יקרא סגיאה דיעקב בשעתא דא״ל קוב״ה אנכי ארד עמך מצרימה. הווי מלאכי עפרא תלת פרסי קרוב לקברי׳ וכר... זכותו וזכות כל הצדיקים יגן עלינו ובעדינו לבטל כל הגזירות קשות מעלינו ולהוציאנו מגלותינו ויבנה ביהמ״ק על ידי משיה צדקינו במהרה בימינו אמן.
segments.en: And therefore through coming to his holy grave and through the weeping and prayers one prays and beseeches there — through this the soul of the true Tzaddik is returned and aroused even more and shines even more below in this physical world. For "the Tzaddikim are found even more in this world after their passing", as stated in the holy Zohar — and the soul of the Tzaddik is more greatly connected in this world and the peace is increased even more — until through this one can draw the entire world to His service. And since peace's way is to clothe itself in bitterness, as explained in the text — therefore one must become very embittered over the passing of the Tzaddik and over one's own great distance from Hashem. And this is the aspect of the weeping and bitterness with which one weeps bitterly at the graves of the Tzaddikim — in order to return and draw the peace that clothes itself in bitterness. And through the bitterness and the broken heart, one then merits joy — which is the aspect of peace — in the aspect of: "for with joy you shall go forth and with peace you shall be led" [Yeshayahu 55:12]. And this is the aspect of the psalms of Tehillim recited there at the graves of the Tzaddikim — which are in the aspect of the ten kinds of melody in which the Book of Tehillim was composed, and which are the source of joy.

segments.he: ע״כ ספר ההשתטחות להגה״ק ר׳ נחמן מטשערין זצ׳׳ל.
segments.en: At the resting place of the Tzaddikim in their holy graves, the holiness of the Throne of Glory shines — which is their inheritance, as it says: "and a throne of glory He shall cause them to inherit" [Shmuel I 2:8]. And therefore there all the places of every single person are included — and one can find there one's own place, until one merits through this to return to Hashem. This is because there shines the holiness of the aspect of the Place of the World — which is the root of all places — and there a person can find the beginning and the start from which he must begin to return to Hashem. And for this reason one travels to the graves of the Tzaddikim on Erev Rosh HaShanah.

segments.he: ועכשיו הוספנו כמה ענינים הנוגעים לענין השתטחות על קכרי צדיקים. להראות אשר שם שורש כל הקדושות, מלוקט מכמה מאמרי חז״ל וזוה״ק ושאר ספרים של צדיקים וקדושים זכותם יגן עלינו אמן.
segments.en: And furthermore: through the journey and travel that each person makes from his place to the Tzaddik — through this he elevates his place to the aspect of the Place of the World, which is the Tzaddik. And this is the aspect of why one travels and journeys to the graves of Tzaddikim — especially before Rosh HaShanah. For in the place where the Tzaddik lies — there is his resting place — in the aspect of: "he shall come in peace, they shall rest upon their resting places." And the primary rest of the Tzaddik is when he is connected and included in the aspect of the Throne of Glory — the aspect of the Place of the World — where there is the primary rest and the inheritance, in the aspect of: "and a throne of glory He shall cause them to inherit." And therefore there at the place of the burial of the Tzaddik, each person merits that he will be judged favorably from above — through the aspect of the Place of the World.

segments.he: וז״ל הרמב״ן בפי הקת דהנפטרים בנשיקה לא יטמאו מן הדין והוא שאמרו צדיקים אינם מטמאים עכדה״ק.
segments.en: The true Tzaddik's entire longing is always to ascend from level to level — and even when he ascends to where he ascends, he is not satisfied with this at all and strives and yearns etc. to ascend more and more. And this is the Tzaddik's service all the days of his life. But it is impossible to ascend from level to level except through a descent before each ascent. And as long as the Tzaddik is alive in this world — even though he is at an exceedingly great level — even so some aspect of descent according to his level exists for him before every ascent. But when he has departed and is in the World to Come, there is no relevance of descent — and the Tzaddik still yearns there each time to ascend more and more. For His greatness, blessed be He, is without limit. But it is impossible to ascend except through descent — and there descent is not relevant, as above.

segments.he: ז״ל רבי׳ בחיי ריש פ׳ אמור והצדיק הזוכה אל המעלה הזאת אין מיתתו ע״י כח המשחית כשאר בגי העולם והנה משה אהרן ומרים זכו אלי׳ שהזכיר בהם הכתוב (במדבר לג) על פי ה׳ והוא מיתת נשיקה אבל במרים לא נאמר על פי ה׳ כי אינו דרך כבוד של מעלה וכו׳ וכן באבות העולם שכתוב בהם בכל מכל כל, גם רבי נו הקדוש ז״ל זכה אלי׳ לפי שברור הדבר מתוך שנתעלה בהשגת החכמה לא היתה מיתתו ע״י המלאך המשחית ודרז״ל בשעת פטירתו של רבי זקף עשר אצבעותיו כלפי מעלה ואמר רבש״ע גלוי וידוע לפניך שיגעתי בעשר אצבעותי ולא נהגתי אפי׳ באצבע קטנה שלי יהי רצון מלפניך שיהא שלום במגוחתי יצתה בת קול ואמרה יבא •:״יום ינוח על משכבו ואמרו בירושלמי כד דמך ר׳ יהודה נשיאה הכריז ר׳ ינאי אין כהונה היום וטעם הדבר מפגי שהכהנים מוזהרין
segments.en: Therefore when someone comes to his holy grave and cries out that Hashem should forgive and pardon him for his many sins and draw him close to His service — the Tzaddik descends to the level of this person who has come to his grave to help him there. And this is counted for the Tzaddik as if he himself descended — and through this the Tzaddik ascends even higher and higher according to his level, in the aspect of descent as the ultimate ascent. For he merits to strive and find even more wonderful and hidden kindnesses — exceedingly hidden — and to reveal them from concealment to revelation in a manner that allows him to help and elevate even this person from that enormous descent he is in now, through the multitude of his sins. And this is the primary delight and joy of the Tzaddik — more than all the pleasures of the World to Come — when he does some eternal good for some person from Yisrael who has descended to wherever he has descended. For this is the primary service of his lifetime and after his passing — for he stands and serves still on high. And the primary service and function is to help Yisrael in general and specifically — primarily to take them out of the distress of the soul and from the depths of each person's descent according to his level. And to reveal new wondrous kindnesses each time — which are the greatness of the Creator, revealed specifically through drawing close and elevating the distant and lowly ones. It follows that specifically through this person who comes from such a deep descent to prostrate at the grave of the Tzaddik — to pray and strive from there to merit complete teshuvah — specifically through him the Tzaddik merits, after his passing, the aspect of descent as the ultimate ascent. And then the Tzaddik ascends in such a great ascent and draws such wondrous kindnesses — until even this distant and lowly one can draw close to Hashem.

The passing of the Tzaddik accomplishes a great rectification in all the worlds more than in his lifetime — for the Tzaddikim are greater in their death than in their lifetimes. For the primary greatness of the Tzaddik in his lifetime and in his death is according to how much he merits to draw the souls of Yisrael close to Hashem — which is the primary delight and joy of Hashem, as our Sages taught: "Did I give you greatness for anything other than for the sake of Yisrael?" And therefore the Tzaddikim are greater in their death than in their lifetimes — for in their death they draw more souls close to Hashem.

The primary engagement through which the Tzaddik works to rectify the souls of Yisrael is specifically at the time of his sleep. For from the Tzaddik's own mind it is impossible to receive — since his mind and daas is so great and elevated that it is impossible to receive from it in any way, except through the Tzaddik lowering himself to the world and setting aside his mind and speaking worldly conversations and story-tales — which is the aspect of sleep — and specifically through this he arouses them to teshuvah and returns them to Hashem. And similarly even when the true Tzaddik reveals Torah to the world — even though it is very lofty Torah and a wondrous and awesome revelation — even so it is the aspect of sleep relative to his own actual attainment, which is so lofty that it cannot be perceived even in thought, certainly not in speech. It follows that the drawing close of Yisrael to their Father in Heaven — which the Tzaddik is always engaged in — is only through the aspect of his sleep. And similarly in the straightforward sense, the sleep of the Tzaddik is at a wondrous level of holiness — for then his holy soul ascends and is included in holy faith, which is the aspect of Malchus [Sovereignty] — and through this a very great and elevated union is made. And through this many fallen sparks are clarified and ascend — and these are the carnal fallen ones. And then those wicked people who are from the root of these sparks of souls are aroused to teshuvah and return to Hashem. Therefore at the time of the Tzaddik's passing — which is the aspect of his long sleep — and then his soul ascends and is included in where it is included — the holy union is greatly magnified. And through this fallen sparks are clarified and ascend more and more in great abundance — until through this many wicked people return to teshuvah. And so it goes throughout all the days of the world until the resurrection — for the souls of the Tzaddikim who have departed are constantly raising up mayin nukvin [feminine waters] to the holy Shechinah, which is the aspect of faith — and through this She clarifies many souls that have fallen without end.

For there are fallen souls that have fallen so low that it is impossible for them to have any rectification in the world except through the soul of the Tzaddik — and specifically through his death and passing — through which a great and supremely elevated union is made. For according to the greatness of the union above, so are many sparks raised from the depths of the kelipas. And this is the aspect of the virtue of the holiness of prostrating at the graves of the holy Tzaddikim — which is a very great thing and very greatly benefits the service of Hashem. To merit to emerge from one's evil and return to Hashem. And this is also the matter of the Hilula of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai that is celebrated on the day of his passing with great joy specifically. For there is no joy and delight before Hashem like the joy when the distant ones draw close and return to Him in teshuvah. And the great Tzaddikim — through whose passing they rectify and return many souls to teshuvah — through this the joy is greatly increased. And this joy is the aspect of the joy of the future at the time of the resurrection. For the Tzaddikim in their death are called living — for the Tzaddik immediately at the moment of his passing goes to his world for good life and for peace, to gather the dispersed and draw close the distant and give them life — eternal life in this world and the next. Through this the joy is greatly, greatly increased.

All the flaws in the world are in the aspect of a flaw in the honor of Hashem — for all the Torah is for the sake of His honor. And when one causes any sin in the world, Heaven forbid — especially the flaw of the bris, which is the primary one — through this His honor is diminished, and the soul is then distanced from the honor. And according to the flaw, so is the distance. And similarly the honor falls, Heaven forbid, to the other nations and the wicked. And there are many aspects without measure in the matter of the flaw of the fall of honor and in the matter of the distancing of the soul from the honor.

Therefore at the place of the graves of the Tzaddikim — where the honor of Hashem gathers — in the aspect of: "the glory of Hashem shall gather you in" [Yeshayahu 58:8] — said about the passing and burial of the Tzaddik, as understood from the words of our Sages. Therefore there is the primary rectification for all flaws — especially for the flaw of the bris. And through the soul returning to the honor — through this one merits to pray with devotion and a wholehearted heart. And this is the aspect of the great arousal at the graves of the true Tzaddikim — where one prays and beseeches with great arousal of the heart and pours one's heart there like water before Hashem. And this is because there the soul draws close to the honor even more — from which prayer flows — prostration with devotion and a wholehearted heart, as explained inside the text.

The immense virtue of the holiness of the graves of the Tzaddikim — how greatly it benefits a person for the rectification of his soul, to take him out of his heavy exile — that is, the exile of the soul, which is the primary exile. This is the aspect of the exile of Egypt which encompasses all the exiles. For the primary redemption from Egypt was through the bones of Yosef, as it says: "and Moshe took the bones of Yosef with him" etc. As understood in the holy Zohar — for the ark of Yosef that was carried at the time of the Exodus from Egypt is in the aspect of the grave of the Tzaddik. And through this was the primary redemption. For the Tzaddik merits to rectify the holy honor in his lifetime to such a degree that at the moment of his passing he is immediately gathered and included in the honor of Hashem, in the aspect of: "the glory of Hashem shall gather you in." And therefore at his holy grave — which is his resting place — the honor of Hashem rests there. And through this all the souls of Yisrael are drawn after this holy honor — which is their root. And through this they merit to emerge from their exile to life and to peace. And they merit to receive a new vitality and a new soul each time through the holiness of this honor.

And this matter of rectification described above encompasses everything. For even Kohanim [priests] who cannot come and prostrate at the graves of the Tzaddikim — if they would need to overshadow also other graves buried near them, or pass over other graves until they get there — this is clearly not to be taken lightly. But it has already been explained elsewhere at length that regarding Kohanim or other people who have some other constraint such that it is truly impossible for them to come to the actual grave of the Tzaddik — it is clear that the holiness of the grave of the Tzaddik, and especially the great Tzaddik who is among the most supremely elevated, certainly extends in its holiness to all who see it. So that one who comes close to the cemetery and merits to see and behold from there the place of the holiness of his burial — and connects his heart and intention to him and leans upon his merit and prays and multiplies supplications and pours his heart like water before Hashem — certainly merits to draw all the wondrous rectifications that flow through the holiness of the graves of the Tzaddikim, as one who merits to pray in full prostration at his actual grave. And there are clear proofs for this from the Talmud and the halachic decisors. And it is well known that this was the custom of the holy Kohanim who were disciples of the Baal Shem Tov of blessed memory.

And it is important to know that the matter of the kabbalistic intentions associated with prostration — as is known — does not apply in our times at all except to rare and supremely elevated individuals. For it is already well known and publicised what the holy Ari, of blessed memory, commanded his holy disciples not to engage in this after his passing — and especially in our times. And we have only to intend simply: to multiply greatly prayer and supplication in the merit of the Tzaddikim and to arouse great mercy there from the Tzaddikim themselves — that they pray for us and arouse great mercy before Hashem upon us and upon all Yisrael. And for this matter, the primary virtue of prostration is only the drawing close and the striving in this through thought, speech, and deed in actual practice.

And anyone who comes with effort and striving and the weariness of travel and lack of money and similar obstacles — and who breaks through all of them for the sake of drawing upon himself some spark and illumination from the holiness and merit of the Tzaddik — even though he cannot actually prostrate at his grave — even so everything is worthwhile for him — to come at least to the area near his holy grave, and gaze with his eyes and direct his heart and connect his thoughts to the holiness of the Tzaddik who rests there. Certainly the holiness of the holy grave extends to all who see it. And even if he stands from a distance, he can request there all his requests and multiply supplications for all that he needs — and certainly his prayer will be accepted. And so it shall be for all — all the holy rectifications as for one who prostrated fully and multiplied supplications at the actual grave of the Tzaddik.

And it is further written in the Midrash Rabbah, Parashas Naso [ch. 14]: in reward for Yosef's restraining his eyes from gazing at the wife of Potiphar and at the women of Egypt etc., the Holy One blessed be He said: "It is upon Me to pay the reward of that eye." How so? The Sages taught that those who ate sanctified offerings in the Temple — those of lesser holiness — ate within the city wall, within the wall of Jerusalem. But Shiloh, which was in the portion of Yosef, one may eat while being able to see [it from any direction]. And from this one understands also regarding the holiness of the grave of the true Tzaddik — who is in the aspect of Yosef — that the primary virtue of his holiness is according to the virtue and level of his holiness in the sanctity of the bris. And the great Tzaddik who merited the sanctity of the bris and the sanctity of the eyes in the ultimate dominion — in particular this Tzaddik who merited to declare that he has no gazing whatsoever in this world — as explained elsewhere — and who disclosed himself something of the greatness of the virtue of his holy grave, and promised etc. etc. — certainly the holiness of his grave extends to all who see it, as described above.

And especially the matter of the custom from ancient times — and so too now and for all future generations, G-d willing — to gather together on Rosh HaShanah and before Rosh HaShanah, especially on Erev Rosh HaShanah, to multiply the recitation of Tehillim and supplications and petitions and teshuvah and prayer and charity at the place of his holy burial — and afterward the entire gathering prays together on Rosh HaShanah. This matter surpasses everything — and through it, high, wondrous, and awesome rectifications are accomplished.
